analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches, and supplied source excerpts against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. These units change documentation, not executable controls. changelog.d/coordinator-traffic-verdict.md:3–5 describes traffic diagnostics, persisted connection timing, and idle-only re-registration with bounded backoff. docs/provider/cli-reference.md:998–1009 (head patch) documents lease expiry, missing verdicts, disconnects, and suppression for stale snapshots or drains. No independently supported security regression appears in this documentation; unchanged surrounding material on encryption, model integrity, caches, logout, qualification, and lifecycle barriers is not a new issue.
Integration must verify the described runtime behavior in ProviderCore/Diagnostics/ServingReadiness.swift and darkbloom/StatusCommand+Traffic.swift: eligibility must reflect current connection-bound authorization rather than cached identity or diagnostic evidence (A-016, TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-058). The re-registration implementation and its coordinator contract remain outside this batch: check grant/challenge invalidation, rejection of late prior-session replies, preservation of revocation and qualification policy (T-053/T-054), retry admission/backoff (T-057), and exclusion during accepted work, terminal usage settlement, model switches, drain, or update. The changelog's claim that registration clears verification retry state is not evidence of a policy bypass without that implementation. No supplied change affects prompt encryption, cache scoping, billing controls, or privileged fan authority.
